Root cause: `objToLocalTS()` in `src/impl/util.js` corrected years 0–99 with `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which first normalized out-of-range month/day overflow inside the 19xx year and only then changed the year. The fix sets year, month and day together (`d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`) so overflow normalizes under the target year's own leap rules. arguments.text: Fixed. Root cause: `DateTime#isInDST()` compared the current offset with probes built via `this.set({ month: 1 })` / `this.set({ month: 5 })`, and `set()` keeps the day of month — so for a 1974 date with day ≥ 6 the "January" probe landed inside the 1974 year-round-DST window (Jan 6 – Oct 27) and returned the same offset, making `isInDST()` false. The January probe is now pinned to `set({ month: 1, day: 1 })`, a genuine standard-time reference. Verified: a full 1974 scan in America/New_York reports DST exactly Jan 6 – Oct 26, a 1248-sample cross-check against an independent reference across 13 zones × 8 years shows 0 mismatches, and the full suite is 892 passed / 2 failed — identical to the pre-fix baseline.
